hints: Focus on two things together, the polarity of each bond and the 3D shape of the molecule, because dipoles can cancel.
Start with CO2, it is linear O=C=O with two identical C=O dipoles pointing in exactly opposite directions.
Now compare CO with its two different atoms, and PH3 with its pyramidal shape and lone pair, to see if their dipoles can cancel.
walkthrough:
**Recall what gives an overall dipole**

A molecule is polar when it has polar bonds whose dipoles do not cancel. Cancellation depends on symmetry of shape.

Rule to use:
$$ \text{overall dipole} = \text{vector sum of bond dipoles + lone pair effect} $$

**Check 1, carbon monoxide, CO**

C and O have different electronegativities, so the $\text{C=O}$ bond is polar. With only two atoms there is no opposite dipole to cancel it.

So $\text{CO}$ has a permanent overall dipole. Statement 1 is correct.

**Check 2, phosphine, PH3**

$\text{PH}_3$ has three polar $\text{P-H}$ bonds and one lone pair on P. Its shape is trigonal pyramidal, like ammonia, not flat.

The three bond dipoles point down to the H atoms and do not cancel symmetrically, so $\text{PH}_3$ has an overall dipole. Statement 2 is correct.

**Check 3, carbon dioxide, CO2**

$\text{CO}_2$ has two polar $\text{C=O}$ bonds, but the molecule is linear: $\text{O=C=O}$.

The two equal dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel exactly:
$$ \vec{\mu}_{total} = \vec{\mu}_{C=O} + (-\vec{\mu}_{C=O}) = 0 $$
So $\text{CO}_2$ has no overall dipole. Statement 3 is incorrect.

**Combine the conclusions**

Statements 1 and 2 only are correct. That matches the combination for 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all polar. CO and PH3 are polar, but CO2 is linear and symmetrical so its bond dipoles cancel to zero.
options.B: Correct. CO is polar because C and O are different atoms, and PH3 is polar because its pyramidal shape prevents cancellation. CO2 is non-polar because its linear shape causes cancellation.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 only are polar. PH3 is indeed polar, but CO2 is not, while CO which is left out is polar.
options.D: Incorrect. This would mean 1 only is polar. CO is polar, but this misses PH3 which is also polar due to its pyramidal shape and lone pair.
